abstract:
The conformal completion contains one distinguished fixed direction, the frozen point, and its length is set by the cosmological constant. [[c:dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry]] This trail follows what that identification buys. [[t]]

The frozen point supplies the extra vector that a known polynomial form of gravity needs, and its wobbles turn out to carry no physics. [[c:dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation]] Where space is empty apart from the cosmological constant, its length cannot change, so dark energy behaves exactly like a cosmological constant. [[c:dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition]]

On one stated condition this becomes a sharp prediction that dark energy never evolves, which a confirmed measurement of evolution would refute. [[c:pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one]] The trail ends with what the framework does not do: it leaves the value of the cosmological constant, and even its sign, as an input. [[c:odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-undetermined-within-series]]
introduction: The walk first builds the geometry of the frozen point, then reads off its prediction for dark energy, and finally asks what kind of number the cosmological constant is. [[t]] Results a step rests on but that are not on the trail are listed at the end. [[t]]
i:dark-energy: These results identify dark energy with the length of one fixed direction in the completed algebra. [[t]]
t:^>dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-ge:
We start from a fact carried over from earlier in the series. [[t]] For a gravitational field on flat spacetime, the vacuum equations amount to one tractor, the frozen point $I$, being parallel (covariantly constant), and with a cosmological constant $\Lambda$ its square length is \[ Q(I) = \Lambda/3 \] [[c:dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry]]

The rotors that leave it fixed form the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$, or the anti-de Sitter group when $\Lambda < 0$. [[c:dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry]]
t:dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geom:
A single direction is not yet enough to write down gravity's action, so the next step builds a partner for it. [[t]] From the frozen point and the canonical tractor $X$ of the conformal geometry comes a second vector, perpendicular to $I$: \[ V = X - \frac{3}{\Lambda}\, I \] [[c:dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point]]

Its length is also set by $\Lambda$, and its rate of change from point to point is exactly the frame that links the six-dimensional tractor space to spacetime. [[c:dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point]]
t:dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-:
That partner vector is precisely what an older reformulation of gravity, due to MacDowell and Mansouri and to Stelle and West, requires. [[c:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector]] Parallelism of $I$ reduces the conformal $SO(2,4)$ structure to the de Sitter group, and the action becomes a square of the curvature of the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field, with no inverse metric anywhere. [[c:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector]]

So it makes sense wherever the connection stays regular, but only while the cosmological constant is nonzero. [[c:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector]]
t:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-:
An action built from two fixed-length vectors raises a worry: their wobbles might be extra fields that matter could feel. [[t]] In the action the two vectors are held to the constraints \[ Q(I) = \Lambda/3 , \qquad \ip{V}{I} = 0 , \qquad Q(V) = -3/\Lambda \] and counting shows nine possible wobbles and nine broken symmetries, matched one to one. [[c:dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation]]

So every wobble is pure gauge, and the graviton gains no extra polarisation. [[c:dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation]]
t:dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-phys:
If the frozen point cannot wobble, its length cannot drift, and that is what dark energy would need to evolve. [[t]] On the Einstein region the frozen point is parallel and the connection preserves lengths, so \[ \partial_a Q(I) = 2\ip{\nabla_a I}{I} = 0 \] and dark energy has pressure equal to minus its energy density, $w = -1$. [[c:dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition]]

Going further needs a stated condition: that the frozen point can be defined in regions full of matter so that it stays parallel there, which the obvious extension does not do. [[c:dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition]]
t:dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration:
Granting that condition turns the result into a registered prediction. [[t]] Dark energy cannot evolve: $w = -1$ exactly, at every epoch. [[c:pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one]]

Any confirmed measurement of a different value at any point in cosmic history would rule the idea out. [[c:pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one]]
t:pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one>dark-ener:
The prediction says the length is fixed; the remaining steps ask what fixes it. [[t]] A conserved number in a physical theory is exactly one of three things: dynamical (D), a parameter of the laws (P), or initial data (I) that varies between solutions; being kinematic (K) is a separate question. [[c:dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are]]

So ruling out the dynamical and kinematic options does not leave initial data as the only possibility. [[c:dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are]]
t:dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exha:
Applying that sorting to the frozen point's length gives a definite answer. [[t]] Under the action exactly as written, $\Lambda$ is fixed before variation, and every solution has \[ H^2 = Q(I) = \Lambda/3 \] on its de Sitter region, so the length cannot change within a solution yet differs between theories. [[c:dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws]]

It is a parameter of the laws, not initial data. [[c:dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws]] Making it initial data would need an extra equation of motion that the action does not provide. [[c:dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws]]
t:dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-:
One might still hope the series' own machinery, the transport that repairs places where division fails, could pick the value. [[t]] When the cosmological constant is zero the frozen point is null, and the transport completes that degenerate space to signature $(2,4)$, supplying a canonical null partner $\varphi$ of $I$. [[c:odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through]]

Every vector orthogonal to the Lorentz frame is then $aI + b\varphi$ with norm $2ab$, and a frozen point of cosmological constant $\Lambda$ is one with \[ 2ab = \Lambda/3 \] [[c:odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through]] So the transport fixes everything about the frozen point except its norm. [[c:odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through]]
t:odd-extensions.transport-constrains-fr:
The last step states the consequence plainly. [[t]] Within the series the norm $\Lambda/3$, sign and magnitude together, is data the transport receives rather than data it produces. [[c:odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-undetermined-within-series]]

This does not mean nothing could fix it, only that the transport does not. [[c:odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-undetermined-within-series]]
conclusion:
The thread runs from the frozen point, through a polynomial action whose extra vectors carry no physics, to a prediction that dark energy never evolves. [[c:pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one]]

No postulate is needed on this stretch, but the prediction rests on one stated condition, that the frozen point extends unchanged into regions full of matter. [[c:dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition]] Under the action as written, the frozen point's length is a setting of the laws rather than initial data chosen for each universe. [[c:dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws]]
